source.title_on_document: Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work

supplement.where: Supplementary Materials appended after the main text: PDF pp. 29-62 (supplement pages 1-34). Code and data on OSF (https://osf.io/kzuge/files/osfstorage, linked on p. 28).
supplement.holds: Table S2 (arm sizes and balance), Table S3 (main quality regression with SEs for both personalized arms, plus small- and large-LLM rater ensembles), Table S4 (alternative evaluation prompts with SEs), Fig. S2 (LLM Elo quality and Elo-tertile creativity), expert human Elo validation (supp. pp. 4-5), all system prompts and the creativity theme-extraction prompt.

paper_design_summary: 331 U.S. Prolific workers with marketing, design, or product experience (analyzed after exclusions from 461 recruited) completed psychometric and creativity measures and an AI-led interview, then wrote a 300-400-word marketing campaign for a fictional lab-grown ribeye startup with a GPT-4o assistant. They were randomized to a generic assistant, a personalized assistant (given their own profile and interview summary), or a partially personalized assistant (given another participant's profile). There was no no-AI arm. Campaigns were scored for quality by a GPT-4o-mini rubric judge (with LLM-ensemble and expert-human Elo checks) and for creativity as embedding distance of extracted themes from the average campaign; 100 AI-only simulated campaigns served as a comparison.

studies.label: Marketing campaign experiment with generic, personalized, and partially personalized GPT-4o assistants

assignment.what_was_assigned: Version of the GPT-4o assistant used while writing the campaign: generic, personalized to the participant, or partially personalized (personalized to another participant)
assignment.quote: In this study, we randomly assigned 331 subjects to work with either a personalized, partially personalized, or generic AI assistant and then tasked them to develop a marketing plan for a fictional startup.
assignment.locator: p. 5, Introduction; also p. 1 Abstract, p. 8 Fig. 1, p. 22 Experimental Design
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 19, Participants: "We re-registered our study design and primary analyses (OSF | CreativityBot ...)", hyperlink https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/QF3G7. The word printed is 're-registered'.

arms.name: Generic AI
arms.description: GPT-4o (temperature 1) prompted to ask focused questions, build on the person's contributions, and give feedback; given the company description and initial campaign idea; no personal information.

arms.name: Personalized AI
arms.description: Same prompt plus a GPT-4o synthesis of the participant's psychological, cognitive, creativity, and demographic profile and a summary of their AI-guided interview on marketing experience and work style.

arms.name: Partial personalization
arms.description: Personalized prompt structure but with the profile and interview summary of another participant in the study (robustness condition).

participants.exclusions: Of 461 recruited, 130 were excluded: 12 failed at least 1 of 2 attention checks, 65 used an AI tool other than the one provided, 42 did not engage with the interview chatbot and the AI task assistant, 11 completed the study in under 30 minutes (p. 19). Several of these exclusions depend on behavior after assignment, and arm counts are given only after exclusions (116/114/101, p. 19 and Table S2). The paper does not report how many people were assigned to each arm before exclusions. The abstract calls the 331 'randomized', but they are the post-exclusion sample. p. 18 also says 'We recruited 331 participants', which conflicts with the 461 on p. 19.
participants.who: Prolific workers based in the U.S. with at least 99 percent approval, selected for self-reported work experience in design or creative, marketing, or product management; mean age 38.7, 49.8 percent female, 73.1 percent with at least a bachelor's degree; 31.1 percent marketing experts, 34.1 percent product experts, 34.7 percent neither.
participants.quote: After applying these exclusion criteria, a sample of 331 individuals was brought forward for analysis with 116 participants randomized to generic AI, 114 to personalized AI, and 101 to partially personalized AI (Table S2).
participants.locator: pp. 18-19, Materials and Methods: Participants; PDF p. 52 (supp. p. 24), Table S2

ai_tool.how_used: Participants chatted freely with the assistant while drafting the campaign (mean 5.8 messages, SD 4.5); the assistant asks questions, builds on ideas, gives feedback, and delivers a 300-400-word campaign brief when asked. No guidance on how to use it was given. The arms differ only in the personal information in the system prompt.

task.description: Write a 300-400-word marketing campaign (go-to-market strategy) for 'Cultivated', a fictional lab-grown ribeye startup, covering five components: context and positioning, target audience, messaging and trust building, channel strategy, success metrics. An initial campaign idea was supplied as optional inspiration. Could also be read as creative_writing (advertising).
task.duration: At least 5 minutes requested; mean 18.9 minutes (SD 14.7) on the task (p. 21). Whole study about 45 minutes (p. 18).

outcomes.name: Campaign quality (GPT-4o-mini rubric score, 1-10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4o-mini (temperature 0) rates each campaign 1-10 using a bespoke rubric on strategic soundness and positioning, messaging and trust building, tactical plan and feasibility; the rubric asks the judge to focus on 'strategic depth, creativity, feasibility, and persuasiveness' (supp. p. 11). OLS on treatment dummies controlling for number of messages sent. Robustness variants: average of 4 small LLM judges (Personalized 0.35 (0.16)*, Partial 0.34 (0.16)*) and 3 large LLM judges (Personalized 0.36 (0.18)*, Partial 0.26 (0.17)) in Table S3; Table S4: simplified criteria (the 1-5 prompt used by human raters) Personalized 0.10 (0.07), Partial 0.10 (0.07); different company 0.09 (0.14); unrelated task -0.04 (0.06); modified criteria 0.50 (0.19)**, Partial 0.44 (0.19)*. LLM pairwise Elo: Personalized beta = 79.7 (SE 35.4, p = 0.02 in Fig. S2B caption; p = 0.03 in text p. 7 and supp. p. 3), Partial 38.6 (SE 34.4, p = 0.26). Interaction model with marketing skills: Personalized beta = 2.4, SE 1.1, p = 0.03; Partial 1.4, SE 1.1, p = 0.21 (Fig. 2A). The paper calls this its 'primary LLM rating metric' (p. 7).

contrasts.reported: Personalized beta = 0.59, SE = 0.21, p = 0.005 (text p. 6); Table S3 GPT 4o-mini column: Personalized 0.59 (0.21)**, Turn Count 0.06 (0.02)**, reference Generic. Arm means and SDs not reported.
contrasts.locator: p. 6, Results; PDF p. 59 (supp. p. 31), Table S3

contrasts.reported: Table S3 GPT 4o-mini column: Partial Personalization 0.56 (0.21)**. In the interaction model with marketing skills: beta = 1.4, SE = 1.1, p = 0.21 (Fig. 2A), which the text p. 7 reports as 'no difference'.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 59 (supp. p. 31), Table S3; p. 7 and p. 9, Fig. 2A

outcomes.name: Campaign quality rated by expert human raters (pairwise Elo)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 200 U.S. Prolific raters in upper or middle management, consulting, or market research each made 10 pairwise comparisons ('Which campaign has better overall quality?') on a random subset of 100 campaigns from the generic and personalized arms only; each campaign rated 39.6 times on average (range 26-55); Elo (start 1500, K = 32). Correlation with LLM Elo on the same 100 campaigns r = 0.72.

contrasts.reported: "no significant difference between treatment conditions (beta = 158.2, p = 0.14), although the results are directionally correct"; marketing skills beta = 22.2, p = 0.01. No SE; split of the 100 campaigns by arm not reported.

outcomes.name: Campaign creativity (embedding distance of campaign themes from the average campaign)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4o extracts 1-3-word distinctive themes from each campaign (positioning, audience, messaging, channel, emotional triggers); themes embedded with text-embedding-3-large; creativity is defined from the cosine similarity between a campaign's themes and the average embedding of all campaigns across treatment conditions (p. 23). Higher score = less similar to the average campaign; the scale (means 31.8-56.5) and the transformation from cosine similarity are not stated. Coded as novelty because each campaign is compared with one common centroid of all conditions, not with other campaigns in its own arm; the paper frames it as homogeneity (p. 10). Paper also reports creativity within quality tertiles (low < 7, medium 7, high 8 on the 1-10 rubric) and within LLM-Elo tertiles (Fig. S2C).

contrasts.reported: All campaigns: Creativity mean personalized 52.3, 95% CI [46.8, 57.8] vs generic 53.7, 95% CI [48.2, 59.2]. No test of this full-sample contrast is printed. Highest quality tertile only: personalized beta = 20.5, SE = 6.5, p = 0.002 (Fig. 2B); top third by LLM Elo: beta = 17.6, SE = 5.5, p = 0.002 (Fig. S2C). Fig. 2B also shows a starred difference in the medium tertile with personalized below generic; no coefficient printed. Subgroup ns not reported.
contrasts.locator: p. 10, 'Personalization as Pathway to Counteract AI-Based Homogenization'; p. 9, Fig. 2B; PDF pp. 53-54 (supp. pp. 25-26), Fig. S2C

contrasts.reported: All campaigns: partially personalized 56.5, 95% CI [51.0, 62.1] vs generic 53.7, 95% CI [48.2, 59.2]. Highest quality tertile only: partial beta = 15.5, SE = 6.6, p = 0.02 (Fig. 2B); top third by LLM Elo: beta = 17.1, SE = 6.5, p = 0.01 (Fig. S2C).
contrasts.locator: p. 10; p. 9, Fig. 2B; PDF pp. 53-54 (supp. pp. 25-26), Fig. S2C

outcomes.name: Creativity of AI-only simulated campaigns vs human-AI campaigns
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same theme-embedding creativity score as S1-O3 applied to 100 campaigns generated by AI alone (simulation; generation procedure not described in detail). All 100 scored 8/10 on quality.

contrasts.control_arm: Human-AI campaigns (generic, personalized, partially personalized arms)
contrasts.reported: AI-only Creativity mean = 31.8, 95% CI [26.8, 36.7]; beta = -21.9, p < 0.001, relative to generic 53.7 [48.2, 59.2], personalized 52.3 [46.8, 57.8], partially personalized 56.5 [51.0, 62.1].

outcomes.name: Length of final campaign (word count)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Computed word count of the submitted campaign (mean 355.4, SD 148.0, range 128-2,217). No vocabulary code fits a plain word count; automated_score used as the nearest.

company_involvement.description: Authors at Northeastern University; 'Authors declare that they have no competing interests.' The Funding section is empty.

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly assigned to one of three GPT-4o assistant configurations (ai_design contrast; no no-AI arm, p. 21). 331 people analyzed (116/114/101), well above 50, although 130 of 461 recruited were excluded, partly for post-assignment behavior. Outcomes are scored on the campaign: an LLM-judge quality score and an embedding-based creativity score of the campaign's themes.

one_line_finding: Personalized vs generic GPT-4o assistant raised LLM-judged campaign quality (beta = 0.59, SE = 0.21, p = 0.005; p. 6, Table S3) but not full-sample embedding creativity (52.3 [46.8, 57.8] vs 53.7 [48.2, 59.2]; p. 10), with a creativity gain only within the top quality tertile (beta = 20.5, SE = 6.5; Fig. 2B).
open_questions: Is the creativity measure (each campaign's theme-embedding distance from the average of all campaigns across conditions) novelty for with_ai, or a diversity measure for across_people? I coded novelty because the centroid is common to all arms.

The significant creativity effects condition on quality tertiles, and quality is itself affected by treatment; only the full-sample arm means with CIs are an unconditioned contrast, and no test of that contrast is printed.
Quality is the paper's primary LLM metric; it is coded usefulness although the rubric asks the judge to weigh creativity. Should it count as overall_creativity?
Arm counts before exclusions are not reported; exclusions (other AI tool use, non-engagement, speed) occurred after assignment and may differ by arm.
The search record says the OSF preregistration planned a no-AI condition; this PDF says no Human Only condition was included (p. 21). Not checked against the preregistration.

The paper reports a partial-personalization quality coefficient of 0.56 (0.21)** in Table S3 while the text (p. 7) says there is 'no difference' with partial personalization, which refers to the interaction model (beta = 1.4, SE = 1.1).
notes: Inconsistencies in the document: p. 18 says 331 recruited, p. 19 says 461 recruited with 331 analyzed; LLM Elo personalization p = 0.03 in text (p. 7, supp. p. 3) vs p = 0.02 in Fig. S2B caption; treatment x skills interaction printed as beta = -0.23, p = 0.11 in text and caption but as '< -0.10, p > 0.11' inside Fig. 2A; Fig. 1 task screen says 'an estimated 2 hours' while the study is described as about 45 minutes. Main quality regression controls for number of messages sent, which treatment affects (personalized beta = -2.3 messages, p. 19). Self-reported outcomes (trust, confidence, feedback, assistance, recommendation, cognitive support types) and conversation-process measures (act/coordinate turns, mediation, embedding distribution shifts of AI responses) are not scored on the campaign and are not listed as outcomes. PDF page numbers equal printed page numbers in the main text; supplement page k is PDF page k + 28.
